_flight: SpaceX Starship Integrated Flight Test 5 (IFT-5 / Flight 5), 2024-10-13, Ship 30 (with Booster 12). Complete controlled reentry over the Indian Ocean, flip, landing burn and splashdown on target. Series window: T+2599 s (first HUD altitude reading of 120 km, entry interface) to T+3923 s (last sample before the flip-maneuver speed bump; landing burn follows). t = seconds of mission time (webcast clock). Speed = webcast HUD 'SPEED' in km/h (Earth-relative as displayed by SpaceX); altitude = HUD 'ALTITUDE', integer km.
_series_tolerance_rule: A simulated series passes a column if, at every t in the reference, |sim-ref| <= max(tol_abs, tol_rel*|ref|). Data precision is much tighter (three independent OCR pipelines agree to ~10 km/h and 1 km); the bands leave room for a simplified game entry model (single ballistic coefficient / L/D, no exact SpaceX bank-angle guidance) and ~1 s clock alignment between sources.

ship_speed_kmh.note: HUD resolution 1 km/h. In the window, Boldz5 vs jordixucla (same clock): median |diff| 8, p95 20, max 28 km/h; Boldz5 vs SofieBrink (clock +2 s): median 3, p95 10, max 12 km/h. Measurement error is negligible; 10%/400 km/h band is for model fidelity. Deceleration peaks ~1.5-1.6 g around T+3690 s (steep speed drop 10000->2000 km/h in ~150 s), where 1-2 s timing error alone gives ~30 km/h, so the relative band matters most there.

ship_alt_km.note: Integer-km HUD (+/-0.5 km quantization). All three OCR sources agree within 1 km at every second (median and p95 diff 0). Band covers quantization plus the lifting-entry altitude plateau (~69 km held from T+3040 to T+3210 s) that a simple model may not reproduce exactly.

entry_interface_t_s.note: First second the HUD shows 120 km (jordixucla agrees within 1-2 s). Ship speed 26639 km/h at that moment (still rising slightly as it falls from ~150 km suborbital apogee).

entry_interface_speed_kmh.note: Precise (three sources within ~15 km/h). Initial condition, should be matched tightly.

peak_speed_kmh.note: Max HUD speed during descent at T+2814 s, alt ~90 km (Boldz5 26756 at 91 km; jordixucla 26756 at 90 km at T+2820). Point where drag starts to exceed the gravity component.

peak_speed_alt_km.note: 89-91 km across sources; depends on vehicle ballistic coefficient and atmosphere model.

altitude_plateau_km.note: HUD holds 69-70 km from ~T+3000 to ~T+3210 s while speed drops 25700->22600 km/h: the lift-supported (bank-controlled) phase of the entry. Loose because it depends on commanded L/D.

t_speed_below_10000_kmh_s.note: Alt 46 km at that time. ~1000 s after entry interface; 60 s band (~6%) for model differences in lift/drag.

t_speed_below_1000_kmh_s.note: Alt 20 km. End of the hypersonic/supersonic deceleration; after this the ship settles to belly-flop terminal velocity.

max_deceleration_g.note: Derived: 10-s central difference of HUD speed, peak ~1.55 g along-track near T+3692 s, 37 km, 5160 km/h. Derived from a differentiated OCR series and HUD speed is not exactly inertial airspeed, hence 30%.

terminal_speed_before_flip_kmh.note: Belly-flop terminal speed at <1 km altitude (T+3915-3923: 343->332 km/h, ~92 m/s). Agrees with jordixucla (370 km/h at 2 km, T+3900). 15% for Cd*A/m modelling.

t_flip_start_s.note: Speed bump 332->336->337 km/h at T+3924-3925 then rapid drop to ~50 km/h by T+3933 (landing burn); HUD altitude already reads 0 km (integer). Entry-interface-to-flip duration = 1324 s.
